findings.text: A global relocation operation is available that moves page table bindings from one virtual interval to another according to a caller supplied control descriptor and returns the amount successfully relocated.

Relocation proceeds from coarse to fine granularity, attempting an upper level transfer when the current span exactly fills that level and otherwise descending to the next level, with huge middle entries split when they cannot move whole and with allocation failure terminating the scan while preserving progress made so far.
The span examined at each step is bounded by the remaining source length and by alignment limits at both source and destination for the granularity under consideration.

Whole table transfer at middle and upper levels is permitted only when the platform advertises support and when neither side carries write protection tracking that lacks remap event delivery, and it requires an empty destination slot and a populated non leaf source slot.
Fallback builds that lack coarse move capability report failure for whole table transfer without altering tables, and one huge upper level fallback additionally raises a one time warning.
Huge upper level transfer relocates the single large entry to the destination slot and invalidates translation caches over the huge span.

Leaf entry relocation preserves soft dirty tracking, adjusts protection state when eventless write tracking is being dropped, discards pure tracking markers in that mode, coalesces consecutive present entries where possible, and invalidates translation caches over the leaf span only when at least one present entry was moved.

Reverse mapping stabilisation is requested for whole table moves and otherwise follows the control descriptor flag, ensuring observers see a consistent old or new view across operations such as truncation and migration.

Start addresses may be pulled back to a table boundary only when the source span reaches that boundary, both sides share the same offset within the table, the start is currently misaligned, and the extended prefix does not intersect an existing mapping, with stack moves allowed to align inside the area.

Progress tracking treats the control descriptor as a cursor that advances both sides by the consumed span, reports completion when the source cursor reaches the source end, and clamps negative progress caused by realignment followed by immediate termination to zero.

Resize classification derives from the absolute size difference, distinguishing unchanged, shrinking and growing requests, while overlap detection compares the old and new intervals and a new address requirement is implied by fixed location or no unmap request modes.

Destination selection honours caller supplied fixed placement and sharing mode through the unmapped area allocator, and memory accounting charges the full new size when the old range is retained and otherwise charges only the size difference, with failure reported when the security reserve check denies the charge and with release returning any prior reservation.

Reverse map locks are held around table alterations when required, address space exclusion is relied upon to make source versus destination table lock ordering safe, distinct source and destination leaf or table locks are nested with single depth annotation, and translation cache maintenance is batched across the leaf scan with a final range invalidation when present entries moved.

Relocation assumes the destination slot was previously released, stacked moves during process image setup may legitimately observe a populated destination when descending from coarse to fine granularity, missing reverse map stabilisation risks missing both old and new entries during concurrent traversal, and recovery with swapped roles must apply the same recursion decision on both sides to avoid encountering tables created by the forward pass.
Table kind enumeration covers normal middle, huge middle, normal upper and huge upper entries.
